summary: The United States admits Visa Waiver Program nationals with an ESTA travel authorization ($40.27, valid 2 years) for stays up to 90 days, lets Canadians visit visa-free for up to 6 months, and requires most other visitors to obtain a B1/B2 visitor visa ($185) at a US embassy; citizens of the Marshall Islands and Micronesia, and Bahamians precleared in the Bahamas, also enter without a visa. Presidential proclamations of June and December 2025 suspend entry on visitor visas for citizens of 38 countries and for holders of Palestinian Authority travel documents, with limited exemptions.

visaTypes.name: ESTA — Electronic System for Travel Authorization

fee.notes: Payable online by card or PayPal. Covers tourism, business and transit under the Visa Waiver Program; only for nationals of VWP countries. The $40.27 is a $10.27 processing fee charged to every applicant, plus $30.00 if the application is approved (the $17 travel promotion fee and the $13 General Fund fee); applicants who are denied are charged only $10.27. DHS's fiscal year 2027 notice raises the fee to $40.62 from 16 October 2026.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least six months beyond your intended stay, unless your country is on the US six-month exemption list, in which case it only needs to be valid for the length of the stay. The list covers most of Europe, the UK, Canada, Mexico, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand, India and many others. It includes every Visa Waiver country except Brunei, but not China, Vietnam, Bangladesh, Kenya or Ghana, for example.

tips.text: Apply for ESTA on the official site esta.cbp.dhs.gov, where the fee is $40.27 ($40.62 from 16 October 2026).

DHS recommends applying for ESTA when you make your travel plans, and an approved travel authorization is required before boarding. CBP encourages travelers entering by land to apply at least 72 hours ahead.
The UK government says visa appointments at the US Embassy in London are limited and advises planning your application as far ahead of travel as possible.
The UK government says medical treatment in the US is expensive, that some hospitals ask non-US residents for a deposit on admission, and advises having adequate travel health insurance.

faq.question: What is ESTA and who needs it?
faq.answer: ESTA is the online travel authorization for the US Visa Waiver Program. Citizens of VWP countries (including the UK, most of Western Europe, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand) must obtain it before boarding. It costs $40.27 — $40.62 from 16 October 2026 under DHS's fiscal year 2027 adjustment — is valid for 2 years (or until your passport expires) and allows stays of up to 90 days.

faq.question: How long can I stay in the US with ESTA?
faq.answer: Up to 90 days per visit, for tourism, business or transit. The ESTA site says that if you are admitted under the Visa Waiver Program you may not change or extend your status.

faq.question: How much does a US visitor visa cost?
faq.answer: The B1/B2 visitor visa application fee is $185. Depending on nationality, a reciprocity issuance fee may also be due when the visa is issued.

faq.question: Do Canadian citizens need ESTA or a visa for the US?
faq.answer: No. Canadian citizens can enter the United States for tourism or business without a visa or ESTA and stay for up to 6 months.

faq.question: Is Romania in the US Visa Waiver Program?
faq.answer: No. DHS designated Romania for the Visa Waiver Program on 9 January 2025, paused implementation on 25 March 2025 and rescinded the designation on 2 May 2025, so Romanian citizens need a B1/B2 visitor visa ($185).
